facts.statement: The genus Thambetochen was described by Olson and Wetmore in 1976.
The genus contains two species: T. chauliodous and T. xanion.
facts.quote: subdivision: *T. chauliodous Olson & Wetmore, 1976 T. xanion Olson & James, 1991

facts.statement: Thambetochen belongs to the family Anatidae.
Thambetochen species were large, flightless ducks with robust legs and small wings.
facts.quote: These birds were large, flightless ducks, with robust legs but small wings

facts.statement: These ducks had beaks with tooth-like lamellae and a diet of plants digested via hindgut fermentation.
facts.quote: Their beaks had tooth-like lamellae and their diet was plants which they digested through hindgut fermentation

facts.statement: Thambetochen likely went extinct when Polynesians colonized the Hawaiian islands.
facts.quote: These birds were likely driven to extinction when the islands were colonised by Polynesians

facts.statement: Thambetochen lived from the Gelasian to the Holocene, between 2.58 and 0 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Gelasian to Holocene (2.58 to 0 million years ago)

facts.statement: Fossils of T. chauliodous were found on Maui and Molokai, while T. xanion fossils were found on Oahu.
facts.quote: Los restos de la primera especie fueron hallados en Maui y Molokai, mientras que la otra fue hallada en Oahu

facts.statement: These ducks evolved in isolation on islands that lacked terrestrial mammals.
facts.quote: which had evolved in isolation, on islands without terrestrial mammals
